scientific_scope: Observed finite scaling of paired compiled checkers on a growing complete certificate property whose successor is produced by an action and effect from the exact checked source. This is neither an asymptotic theorem nor a claim about all neural systems.

growth_requirements: complete_obligations strictly grow across points and trace steps
every emitted transition checksum forces source action effect and successor
the observed action request is the proposal-channel request without rewriting
target register length follows the observed request; for this family's advance-zero proposals it equals source register length
at least one local cone transports a nonempty fragment set
at least one extended cone recalculates a nonempty fragment set

parameters.determinism: The family, transition producer, schedule and both compiled checkers are deterministic.

uncertainty.failed_run_policy: Every failure remains in raw_runs and makes the gain verdict false for its point.

accounting.publication: Raw rows, cumulative and amortized totals, all failures, transition checksums and state readouts are mandatory.

practical_gain_rule.name: causal-complete-property-cumulative-incremental-gain
practical_gain_rule.decision: Gain is true only if every repetition completes and median initialization-plus-incremental cumulative time is at most 80 percent of the full recheck at every assessed point.

resource_budget.failure_policy: Timeout, memory excess and rejection are published as unfavorable observations.

negative_control.required_outcome: nonzero exit before an accepted observation

interpretation_rules: v11 remains a historical negative result and is never reclassified.
All finite costs are observations, not Lean theorems.
No asymptotic form is inferred from five finite points.
Fragment reuse and elapsed-time gain are distinct claims.
The confirmatory result file is written once and never overwritten.
The protocol must be frozen at a recoverable clean commit before the run.
